title: Platform Systems & Services - Team Wiki, Runbooks, Dashboards, and Roadmap
author: Asha Patel
summary: Canonical Platform team reference: inventory of systems & services, how-tos for common platform tasks, dashboard & alert standards, operational runbooks, recent retrospectives and action items, and a prioritized roadmap for 2026. Intended as the single-source-of-truth for oncall, SRE, and platform engineering work.
content:
Overview

This page consolidates Platform team knowledge: service inventory, operational playbooks, monitoring and alerting standards, runbooks for common incidents, retrospective action items, and the team roadmap. Use this doc for runbook links, oncall handoff notes, and quick how-tos for day-to-day platform work. Keep changes small and peer-reviewed; major structural changes must include reviewers and a short ADR.

1) Systems & services inventory (high level)

| service | owner | SLA / SLO | description | canonical runbook |
|--------|-------|----------:|-------------|------------------|
| edge-api-gateway | platform-edge | 99.95% p99 latency < 120ms | Public API ingress, routing and auth. Responsible for routing to model-serving clusters. | /runbooks/edge-api-5xx |
| model-serving-runtime | eng-serving-runtime | 99.9% availability | High-throughput GPU inference runtime (CUDA/cuDNN kernels). Supports dynamic batching and KV cache. | /runbooks/model-serving-degraded-throughput |
| job-orchestrator | eng-platform | 99.9% job success rate | Batch and async job orchestration (embeddings builds, evals). | /runbooks/job-orchestrator-failures |
| observability-platform | eng-platform | 99.9% write availability | Metrics, logs, traces (Prometheus, Cortex, Loki, Tempo). | /runbooks/observability-write-errors |
| secrets-kms-proxy | security | 99.99% | KMS key proxy for customer-managed keys (on-prem & cloud) | /runbooks/kms-proxy-unavailable |

Notes: owners are primary on-call rotation contacts. SLA/SLO shown are target values; see individual service pages for detailed SLI definitions and measurement windows.

2) How-tos (common ops tasks)

- Deploy a new microservice (canary pattern):
  1. Create PR with Helm chart changes under charts/<service>. Include resource limits and podDisruptionBudget.
  2. Add a dashboard stub in Grafana: panels for p95/p99 latency, error rate, request rate, CPU/GPU usage.
  3. Add Prometheus scrape config and instrument metrics (request_total, request_errors, request_latency_seconds_bucket).
  4. Add runbook stub referencing the new service and assign owner.
  5. Rollout via CI pipeline: feature -> canary (10%) -> 50% -> 100% with 10m observation windows.

- Add an alert:
  1. Draft alert rule in prometheus/rules/platform-rules.yaml with runbook link. Use labels: team=platform, severity=sev2 (adjust as needed).
  2. Target thresholds: severity mapping (see below). Include for alert: description, runbook, playbook link, and suggested remediation steps.
  3. Open PR and request reviews from owner and observability. After merge, verify alert fires using alertmanager/silence test.

- Oncall handoff checklist:
  - Share active incidents and current mitigations.
  - List planned maintenance and silences.
  - Note any flaky alerts to mute or refine.
  - Confirm Grafana/PagerDuty access and escalation policy.

3) Dashboards & alerting standards

Dashboards (canonical names):
- Platform / Edge / API Gateway - Overview
- Platform / Serving Runtime - Performance
- Platform / GPU Fleet - Utilization & OOMs
- Platform / Observability - Ingestion Health

Panel minimums for service dashboards:
- Request rate (requests/s)
- Error rate (%) and 5xx counts
- Latency histogram (p50, p95, p99) and heatmaps for long tail
- Resource utilization (CPU, memory, GPU util, GPU memory)
- Queue/backpressure depth (if applicable)

Alert severity mapping (standard):
- sev1 (pager duty, phone) — Production outage or customer-impacting >10% errors or p99 latency > 2x SLO for >5m.
- sev2 (pager duty, no phone) — Significant degradation: elevated error rate or latency breach at p95 for >10m.
- sev3 (email, slack) — Non-urgent: single-instance problems, repeated job failures, or resource pressure warnings.

Alert routing: label team=<owner> and route in Alertmanager by team. All alerts must include runbook link. Use silence for planned maintenance only and document in oncall handoff.

4) Operational runbooks (examples & templates)

Runbook naming convention: runbooks/<service>-<symptom>.md (example: runbooks/edge-api-5xx.md). Each runbook must include: summary, detection criteria, immediate mitigation steps, root-cause diagnosis commands, rollback steps, post-incident actions, and owner.

Example: Edge API 5xx spike (summary)
- symptom: sudden spike in 5xx rate > 5% of requests for 3m and p95 latency > 2x baseline.
- immediate mitigation (1-5, numbered):
  1. Check Grafana panels: API Gateway - Overview, Backend error counts.
  2. Hit /health endpoints for upstream model-serving clusters.
  3. If a specific backend returns errors, disable route with weight=0 via routing-control (console CLI: platform route set-weight --service backend-x --weight 0).
  4. If cascading, enable fallback model-variant route (model-serving supports variant=v1-fallback).
  5. If upstream dependency (e.g., KMS) is degraded, switch to cached keys where safe and follow KMS runbook.
- diagnosis commands: kubectl get pods -n platform -l app=edge-api -o wide; promql: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="edge-api",status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (instance)
- owner: platform-edge team oncall.

Example: GPU node OOMs (summary)
- symptom: node-exporter OOM logs + pod restarts + GPU memory allocation failures.
- immediate mitigation: cordon node, scale up temporary GPU pool, move critical traffic to healthy nodes.
- diagnosis: check dmesg, nvidia-smi pmon, kubelet logs for OOMKilled containers.

5) Recent retrospectives & action items (last 3)

- Retrospective: Q4 2025 - Canary rollout incidents
  - Problem: two rollouts missed canary watch windows leading to increased error exposure.
  - Action: Add mandatory CI gate that prevents 50->100% rollout without successful 30m canary checks (owner: eng-platform, due: 2026-01-15).
  - Status: completed.

- Retrospective: Jan 2026 - Observability ingestion backlog
  - Problem: Cortex write queues saturated during eval-harness runs.
  - Action: Implement per-tenant rate limiting in Cortex and add pre-run quota checks for large eval jobs (owner: eng-platform + applied-ml, due: 2026-03-01).
  - Status: in_progress.

- Retrospective: Feb 2026 - GPU OOM storms during model onboarding
  - Problem: onboarding jobs used unquantized models causing memory spikes.
  - Action: Create 'onboarding-limits' preset that enforces quantization/sequence-length caps and requires review by eng-serving-runtime before scheduling on GPU pool (owner: eng-serving-runtime, due: 2026-04-01).
  - Status: planned.

6) Platform roadmap (prioritized, Q2-Q4 2026)

- Q2 2026 (near-term):
  - Observability: shard Cortex write path and add tenant-level backpressure (owner: eng-platform).
  - Canaries: implement CI gate for automated canary verification and rollback (owner: eng-platform).
  - Runbooks: standardize runbook template and add automated runbook links to alerts (owner: eng-sre).

- Q3 2026 (mid-term):
  - Dedicated autoscaler: support GPU spot + reserved mixed pool with predictive scaling (owner: eng-infra).
  - Cost tooling: integrate Redwood Optimize suggestions into console for batch/serving differentiation (owner: product).

- Q4 2026 (longer-term):
  - Private deployment ops: hardened onprem packaging and offline update path for air-gapped customers (owner: eng-private-deployments).
  - Increased SLO coverage: expand p99 observability to more internal critical paths and add SLA reporting dashboards (owner: eng-platform).

Roadmap notes: each roadmap item must have a short RFC/PRD attached and include acceptance criteria and rollout plan before development starts.

7) Team wiki structure and conventions

Primary sections (page path conventions):
- /eng-platform/team-wiki — team charter, oncall rotation, contact list, meeting rhythms.
- /eng-platform/runbooks — operational runbooks (one file per symptom).
- /eng-platform/dashboards — dashboard templates and panel library.
- /eng-platform/deployments — deployment patterns, helm charts, and cluster topology.
- /eng-platform/retrospectives — postmortems and action tracker.

Naming & PR conventions:
- File names: short, dash-separated, include year only when needed (e.g., onboarding-limits.md).
- Edits: all substantive changes require at least one reviewer from owner or eng-sre.
- Deprecation: mark pages with label deprecated and add replacement link.

8) Contacts & ownership quick reference

- Platform lead: Asha Patel (asha@redwood.ai)
- Observability owner: Emily Zhang (emily@redwood.ai)
- Serving runtime: Jonah Lee (jonah@redwood.ai)
- Oncall escalation: see PagerDuty schedule (link internal)

Appendix: templates and CLI snippets

- Runbook template (header):
  - title: short descriptive
  - owner: team + primary oncall
  - detection: promql / logs conditions
  - mitigation: immediate steps
  - diagnosis: commands / dashboards
  - rollback: if applicable
  - post-incident: followup tasks

- Common commands:
  - Check edge API pods: kubectl get pods -n platform -l app=edge-api -o wide
  - Prometheus query: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="edge-api",status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (instance)
  - Route weight: platform route set-weight --service backend-x --weight 0 --env prod

Edit history and governance:
- This page is maintained by the Platform team with quarterly reviews. Small improvements can be merged directly; structural changes require reviewer approval.

If you have additions or corrections, open a PR against the team-wiki directory and assign one of the reviewers listed at the top.
